correctness.rationale: The full conditional law follows from signed primitive excursion counts. Catalan convolution normalizes the split; the exact finite formula for Z_{n,k} follows by Lagrange inversion. For any target composition, cyclic preimage counting gives W(y)k(2n-k-1)/[(k+1)(n-k)Z_{n,k}], exactly W(y)/Z_{n,k+1}. A single split proves majorization; 2ab>=2 proves sharp quadratic drop. CHECK.py recomputes exact kernels n<=10 and enumerates all bridges n<=6, with both independent verifications passed; finite tests support rather than replace proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The explicit transition with one split, random cyclic rotation and exact output law proves a stronger, truly multivariate statement. It is not asserted that all scalar Schur-convex moment inequalities are independently novel. No inspected stronger prior result supplies the simultaneous refinement; an undiscovered general fragmentation theorem remains a historical risk.

originality.rationale: The relevant primary papers derive unconditional ranked-excursion laws (Csáki–Hu; Lindell–Holst) and the precise fixed-return Catalan composition mass (Serlet). Their inspected mathematical statements do not provide the explicit cross-k cyclic one-block fragmentation and simultaneous majorization. Earlier size-biased marginal ordering yields related scalar inequalities but not an all-coordinate samplewise refinement; the present claim is explicitly about the latter. Historical priority against generalized forest fragmentation remains noncertified.
residual_risks: Broader tree-fragmentation and renewal-composition literature may contain a representation equivalent to this exact kernel; priority has not been independently certified.
A fixed-k Catalan composition mass and some scalar ordering consequences were known; these are explicitly not credited as new findings.

value.rationale: A natural finite-sample conditioning (number of returns to the origin) admits a concrete all-level Markov coupling of entire excursion-length partitions. The samplewise majorization yields all ranked-tail and Schur-convex inequalities from one structural argument and the sharp universal quadratic decrement 2, relevant to duration concentration and bridge pinning. This is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor a consequence of mere finite enumeration.
